note: One file per line. Durations are MEASURED with ffprobe after generation, never estimated — the driver reads durations.json and holds each beat for its real length plus a 0.45s breath. No line mentions a transaction or a signature: this app has no blockchain component. tryon/matchwhy line texts are swapped relative to the original plan: the card sits on its detail side for the tryon span and shows the render for the matchwhy span, so each line now describes the screen it plays over.

lines.text: This is SWIPEFIT. Every card you are about to see is a real garment, rendered onto a real person's body. And one skin scan decides which garments you see at all.
Online, you buy clothes on a model who is not you. The colour that suits them may fight you, and you find out after it arrives. SWIPEFIT moves that decision to before the purchase.
First, the one thing a skin scan cannot tell us: what you actually want to wear. It is asked once, and it filters the catalogue rather than profiling you.
The scan needs two photos, because a face reading and a full-body try-on want genuinely different framing. On a real phone you take them. Here, three bundled people span the tone range.
I will use the deep-tone person deliberately. Most colour tools misread deep skin as cool. This one does not, and I want that on camera.
This is a live call to YouCam Skin AI, happening now. Nothing here is pre-baked — the network request is genuinely in flight.

Warm, and deep. Deep Autumn. The API returns colour only — no undertone field exists. Every warm-cool judgement is derived here, in CIELAB, against a neutral axis that moves with lightness. That curve is exactly why this reads warm instead of cool.
Sixty pieces from nine real brands, re-sorted around that one reading. Not filtered — re-ordered. A shopper who only ever saw flattering colours could not tell the sort was doing anything.
Tap the card and it tells you why it scored what it scored, in words. Terracotta runs warm, the same direction as this person's undertone.
And this is the claim. That garment, rendered onto that body, through YouCam Apparel Virtual Try-On. Not a stock photo, not a mock-up.
Notice the brand is hidden. Most people buy the label before they judge the garment, so SWIPEFIT hides it until after the decision. That single choice is what makes the next number possible.
Swipe right, and only then does the brand reveal itself. The bag fills, and the deck counts down.
Swipe left on something that fights the reading, and it is gone. The sort is doing real work, not decorating a random order.
Now I turn the label back on, and keep swiping. That gives the console the two halves it needs: decisions made blind, and decisions made knowing the brand.
The bag spans brands, because a shopper does not think in shops. Each brand keeps its own colour across the whole app.
Now the part the API cannot do on its own. It takes one garment per call — so SWIPEFIT chains it. The rendered top becomes the body the trousers go onto, and you get a complete outfit on yourself.
There is no payment here, and there is not meant to be. SWIPEFIT opens the brand's own product page and takes no cut. That is what makes brands partners rather than competitors.
Every figure on this screen is measured from the swipes I just made on this device. Nothing is simulated, and nothing is a placeholder.

And this is the measurement no retailer can run on their own shop. Keep rate with the label hidden, against keep rate with it shown. In an ordinary store the shopper can always see whose product they are holding, so brand pull and garment appeal arrive fused. Hide the label, and the gap between those two numbers is what the name is worth.
SWIPEFIT. The face decides what you wear. Built on YouCam Skin AI and Apparel Virtual Try-On, with the colour science implemented rather than gestured at. Thanks very much for watching.

decisions.supabase: Not required. The in-app brand console computes from local swipe state; only the website console reads Supabase, and that is out of scope for this take.
decisions.voice: macOS `say` voice Samantha. Kokoro is not installed and pulling in torch on a disk with 7.5GB free the night before submission is a bad trade.
decisions.length: All 19 beats kept, narration trimmed for pace.
